Maladaptive Strategies.value: control eating strictly to feel in control
I imagine getting revenge on the people responsible
go along with whatever others want to feel safe

Threat.value: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
Even when others tell me I am safe I find it impossible to believe it
Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger

Memory.value: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.
When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel isolated and set apart from others
I feel permanently humiliated by what happened
Somebody else would not have gotten into this situation

vignette: Rohan's eyes still scan the surroundings with a mixture of vigilance and unease, a habit formed during the 30 days he was held captive by an armed group while working as a park ranger in a remote area. It had been two years since his release, but the memories of those four weeks continued to haunt him. He recalls the sound of boots outside his makeshift cell, the feeling of being at the mercy of his captors, and the helplessness that came with it. The experience left an indelible mark on Rohan's life. He became increasingly self-conscious about being seen in public, often finding excuses to avoid social gatherings or events where he might be recognized. The mere sight of people in uniform triggered a cascade of emotions, transporting him back to the moments when his captors would taunt him, wearing their military fatigues as a symbol of power and control. Rohan's relationship with his partner, Nalini, began to suffer as well. He became withdrawn, struggling to connect with her on an emotional level. The memories of his captivity made it difficult for him to trust others, even those closest to him. "How can I be sure she won't leave me or betray me?" he would think to himself, the fear lingering like a shadow. To cope with these feelings, Rohan turned to maladaptive strategies that provided temporary comfort but ultimately exacerbated his distress. He began to restrict his eating, carefully controlling every morsel that entered his body as a way to feel in control of at least one aspect of his life. Revenge fantasies also crept into his thoughts, with vivid scenarios where he would exact punishment on those responsible for his captivity. Rohan's work as a park ranger became increasingly challenging. He found himself people-pleasing, acquiescing to the demands of others without question, in an attempt to avoid conflict or rejection. However, this only served to erode his sense of self-worth and confidence. As Rohan navigated his daily life, he was constantly on edge, waiting for the other shoe to drop. The slightest movement nearby would startle him, sending his heart racing as if he were back in captivity. He couldn't shake off the feeling that danger lurked around every corner, even when Nalini reassured him of his safety. Memories of the event continued to haunt Rohan, often resurfacing as snapshot moments - vivid, frozen images that replayed in his mind like a gruesome slide show. The pain he experienced during those 30 days would return with each recollection, making it difficult for him to distinguish past from present. There were times when he recalled the events with a detached numbness, feeling as though they had happened to someone else. Rohan couldn't help but feel isolated and set apart from others, like an outsider looking in on a world that seemed to be moving forward without him. The experience had left him permanently humiliated, his self-esteem shattered by the feelings of powerlessness. He often compared himself unfavorably to others, convinced that someone else would have handled the situation differently. The cumulative weight of these experiences finally brought Rohan to seek help. He realized that he couldn't continue living in a state of constant hypervigilance, unable to connect with those around him or find solace in his own thoughts. As he sat in the therapist's office, he looked down at his hands, now trembling slightly as he recounted the memories of his captivity. "I just want to feel safe again," he whispered, his voice barely audible over the din of his own fears.
